thought.text: Cloned. Now configure and build GDAL 3.6.2 in the background.

reasoning_content:
Alright, let's configure and build GDAL 3.6.2. Use a minimal feature set to speed up the build. The Python bindings are built separately by the pip package (swig), so we only need the C library and headers. Let's configure with cmake:

```
cmake -S gdal-src -B gdal-build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF -DBUILD_GDAL_SWIG=OFF ...
```

GDAL's cmake options: GDAL_USE_*. By default it auto-detects the system libraries (geos, proj, curl, tiff, zlib, sqlite3?). sqlite3-dev — need to check whether it's already installed. libgeos-dev and libproj-dev are already installed. Let's keep it minimal: GDAL_USE_CURL, GDAL_USE_GEOS, GDAL_USE_PROJ, GDAL_USE_TIFF, GDAL_USE_ZLIB. Disable everything else to speed up the build: -DGDAL_USE_GEOTIFF=OFF? geotiff comes with tiff. There are tons of drivers. To be safe, we could also build with defaults minus the heavy stuff (postgresql, mysql, etc. not installed so they'll be disabled automatically). Actually, auto-detection means it'll only enable what's available. No problem.

Building on 8 cores: roughly 3–6 minutes. Then make install (installing to /usr/local takes precedence over /usr). After installation, the python GDAL build will use gdal-config from /usr/local/bin.

Note: the pip gdal 3.6.2 build compiles the swig wrappers against the installed headers — with GDAL 3.6.2 headers it should succeed.

One consideration: the system's libgdal3.4.1 (from the package) and the /usr/local/libgdal.so.32 from source. Both can coexist. The venv will link against /usr/local via gdal-config. At runtime, the venv's _gdal .so will be linked against libgdal.so.32 (from /usr/local). We need to either run ldconfig or set LD_LIBRARY_PATH. make install + ldconfig handles that (does /usr/local/lib exist in the default ld path? /usr/local/lib is listed in /etc/ld.so.conf.d/libc.conf, yes).

Let's do the configuration and build in the background with nohup, logging the output to /tmp/gdal_build.log.

action.command:
cd /tmp && nohup bash -c 'cmake -S gdal-src -B gdal-build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF -DGDAL_USE_CURL=ON -DGDAL_USE_GEOS=ON -DGDAL_USE_PROJ=ON -DGDAL_USE_TIFF=ON -DGDAL_USE_ZLIB=ON -DPNG_WANT_SIMPLE=ON > /tmp/gdal_cmake.log 2>&1 && cmake --build gdal-build -j8 >> /tmp/gdal_cmake.log 2>&1 && cmake --install gdal-build >> /tmp/gdal_cmake.log 2>&1 && ldconfig >> /tmp/gdal_cmake.log 2>&1 && echo GDAL_BUILD_OK > /tmp/gdal_build_done.txt' > /tmp/gdal_nohup.log 2>&1 &
echo "started $!"
